entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Also heard Mr. Swajeet Ubeja, learned Panel Lawyer,
appearing for the State/respondent No.1.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the entire prosecution case is misconceived, as the dispute between the complainant and the petitioners is essentially civil in nature arising out of agreements to sell immovable properties.
It is submitted that no element of cheating or dishonest intention at the inception of the transaction is made out against the petitioner.

It is further contended that the complainant himself had entered into agreements to sell with the petitioners in respect of certain properties, but subsequently, on account of financial transactions, blank cheques and signed blank stamp papers were taken from petitioner No.2 by the complainant as security for loan purposes.
The said documents have been misused by the complainant to lodge a false criminal case against the petitioners.

Learned counsel submits that even assuming the allegations of the Smt. Sangeeta Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/29690787/
1 complainant to be correct in toto, the same would, at the highest, give rise to a civil liability for enforcement of contract or recovery of money, but would not constitute an offence of cheating under Section 420 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Smt. Sangeeta Gupta vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled principle of law that mere breach of contract cannot give rise to criminal prosecution unless fraudulent or dishonest intention is established at the time of entering into the contract, which is conspicuously absent in the present case.

It is further submitted that the Investigating Agency, without properly appreciating the civil nature of the dispute, has mechanically filed charge-sheet vide Final Report No. 594/2025 dated 06.06.2025, and the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur, has erred in taking cognizance of the offence under Section 420/34 of IPC vide order dated 09.06.2025.
The said order of cognizance is liable to be set aside.
As such, the continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners amounts to abuse of the process of law and is liable to be quashed.

The learned State counsel endorses the said fact that the charge-sheet has been submitted before the trial Court concerned as well as order taking cognizace has been passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur vide order dated 09.06.2025.
In view of the above, issue notice to the respondents by ordinary process as well as speed post.
Learned State counsel appears and accepts notice on behalf of respondent No.1 therefore, issuance of notice to the State/respondent No.1, is dispensed with.
Issue notice to respondent No.2 by ordinary and speed post.
Process fee be paid as per Rules.

Four weeks' time is granted to the learned counsel for the respondents to file their reply-affidavits and thereafter, two week's time is granted to the learned counsel for the petitioner to file rejoinder- affidavit.
List the matter thereafter.

Till the next date of listing, the further proceedings of Criminal Case No.20593/2025 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Bilaspur (C.G.) insofar as relates to the petitioner, shall remain stayed.

Sd/- Sd/- -
 (Bibhu Datta Guru) (Ramesh Sinha)
